ron.method: Japanese performance cars are rated on premium. JIS K 2202 sets premium at 96 RON minimum; JAMA says premium as sold is about 98–100 RON and an OEM engine engineer puts it at 98–99.5 (clicccar, 2020). 99 sits in both ranges.

sources.title: Gasoline explained - octane in depth - U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA)
sources.note: Premium (the highest octane fuel—generally 91–94) ... The large number on the yellow gasoline pump octane label is the minimum octane rating. (R+M)/2 Method on the label refers to the octane testing method used, where R is Research Octane Number and M is Motor Octane Number.

sources.title: ORNL/TM-2016/42 Summary of High-Octane, Mid-Level Ethanol Blends Study (ORNL/NREL/ANL, July 2016)
sources.note: In the United States, the octane number at the retail pump is given as the anti-knock index (AKI), the average of the RON and the motor octane number (MON), AKI = ½(RON + MON). ... Note that in Figures 3, 4 and 5 the fuel economy (E0 MPGeq) represents miles per gallon normalized to the 97 RON E0 (93 AKI) fuel based on lower (volumetric) heating value.

ron.method: US pumps post AKI = (RON + MON)/2; premium is generally 91–94 AKI (EIA). ORNL test fuels pair 93 AKI with 97 RON and 88 AKI with 91 RON, so the lowest premium grade, 91 AKI, is taken as about 95 RON. Some US figures (LS1 F-body, 87 AKI regular) were rated on less.
